<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via translateDashboard (symbol, a top-level function), translateReport (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1dbe3dd17f558a08d0ba9ce0f6bd88fa60c84003` — the merge of head `8ad569b7e57e1bebcb6c0875d75b6ff8a96661be` into base `441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1dbe3dd17f558a08d0ba9ce0f6bd88fa60c84003 && git checkout 1dbe3dd17f558a08d0ba9ce0f6bd88fa60c84003
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590 8ad569b7e57e1bebcb6c0875d75b6ff8a96661be && git checkout -B drift-repro 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590 && git merge --no-ff 8ad569b7e57e1bebcb6c0875d75b6ff8a96661be

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 441a0d7d4d8b62841564da38a2db0097286af590` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

L1 (L1-e) on head `e2d307a1e11993f86e16ad2ed4078d004907a187`, card #36373: **REWORK**. Two items are owed. Item 2 is text. Item 1 is evidence, and it changes code only if the run finds something. The same kind of run on #36405 found two real bugs.

**Owed**
1. **One live run, as the card's acceptance asks.** The panels are shown only through a Vite harness over a fetch stub, and the heading fix is pinned only by a unit test. The value of this card crosses the `/meta` boundary twice: a panel edit is stored as `{ default: SOURCE, 'zh-CN': EDIT }`, and `translateReport`/`translateDashboard` must then serve it. Against a fresh local backend and the console, with HotCRM installed, report readings for:
   - Open 「各阶段商机」 and press 编辑. The heading and subtitle stay Chinese, and the panel reads 数据来源 商机指标 / 指标 金额 · 合计、平均赢单概率 · 平均 / 分组 阶段 / 柱状图.
   - The panel's text contains none of `total_amount`, `stage`, `bar`, `opportunity_metrics`, `RLS`, 维度, 度量.
   - In English, the labels are English with no machine names.
   - Studio's panel for the same report and the same dashboard widget uses the same words.
   - On a self-built, untranslated app, the labels are the author's text.
   - **The round trip:** edit the report name in zh-CN and Save, then reload. The page and the name box show the edit, English still shows the source, and the network shows the stored map.
   - Live screenshots replace the harness ones.
2. **Two sentences say more than the resolver does.** The changeset says "The server resolves that entry ahead of the translation bundle, so the edit is what the page shows after save." `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx` says "the server serves that entry ahead of the translation bundle". `inlineEntryOverridesPackagedBase` returns `false` when no packaged base is supplied, and the PR's own control pin says so ("an edit to an own-package report with a bundle entry still loses to that bundle"). In that case the edit is stored but not what the page shows. Scope both sentences to the packaged-base case, as `i18n-standard.mdx` already does correctly.
   - A question for the seat or L2, not an L1 finding: in that same case the panel accepts an edit that will not show after Save, with no word to the admin. Whether the panel should say so, or the case should be left as is, is a design call. I am raising it, not ruling on it.

**Checklist (passes)**
- Shape (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36420`): open, draft, base `main`, `Fixes #36373`, no keyword near another card. Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, both with reasons. `Skills-docs: none` is true: I re-ran the stated grep, and `skills/` names none of `translateReport`, `translateDashboard`, the two inspectors, or "inline locale map". At this head `Check Changeset` completed `success` (an earlier run was still in progress when the seat asked). Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are `success`.
- `Fixes` is right once (1) holds. Items 1–7 are built, in all three places (the runtime report editor, the dashboard widget bar that #36372 reuses, and Studio). The 不做 list is respected: the panels keep their structure and items, objects are not offered as a data source, and the dataset designer is untouched.
- Scope: the claim amendment (7076914692) names the spec resolver. The `metadata-form-zh-cn.ts` rewording is inside the panels the card names, and the body marks it (⟨36373⟩). The seven moved tests follow the new wording.
- Resolver, read against the diff:
  - `inlineEntryFor` takes the exact tag, then the base tag, and never `default`.
  - `inlineEntryOverridesPackagedBase` is true only when the entry differs from the base's own entry, so a package that ships the same map keeps its bundle.
  - `translateDataset` is untouched (ADR-0149), with a pin showing a dataset member's map still loses.
  - The census of inline maps across the three repos found 0 on these props, so no stored document changes reading.
  - The ablation (precedence → `false`, 3 of 24 red) is a real positive control.
- Docs: `i18n-standard.mdx` (precise, including the no-base case) and `dashboards.mdx` (the binding section wording, labels-only) are true sentence by sentence. For `reports.mdx` and the changeset, see item 2. The rest of the changeset is true against the diff.
- Out-of-scope `carrier: none`: the en report form rows still read the spec's English ("Dataset binding"). That is wording, not a machine name, so the card's en acceptance line is not broken. Whether it gets a card is the seat's call.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e2d307a1e11993f86e16ad2ed4078d004907a187`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/spec/src/system/i18n-report.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/servedLabel.ts

Inputs read: card #36373 body and its five comments (two claims, triage, notification, os-dev-report 7078791835), PR #36420 body and its one comment, the net diff against `main` (30 files, merge base `97b9d1e6`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read in the tree at the head, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts`, `ui/packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, and ruling record 6631250894 on #30062, which the resolver cites.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. `I18nLabelSchema` already takes a string or an inline locale map on a report `label` and `description` and on a widget `title`. No schema file is in the diff. Right.
- Public surface of `@objectstack/spec`: no export added, removed or renamed. `inlineEntryFor` and `inlineEntryOverridesPackagedBase` are module-private. `scalarOverridesPackagedBase` and `valueOverridesPackagedBase` are untouched, so the object fold in `@objectstack/objectql` that imports the exported predicate keeps its rule. Right.
- Served output: changed for three slots. Before, a map on a report `label` or `description` or a widget `title` never counted as changed, so the catalog answered whenever it had a key. Now the map's entry for the requested locale is served when a packaged base exists and the entry differs from the base's entry. This is a change of meaning, and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is the right kind. Right.
- Existing stored documents: a stored override whose map carries an entry for a locale that differs from the base does read differently in that locale. The census in the PR body covers the packaged sources of three repos (0 maps on these slots). It cannot see override rows in a deployment. The semantic arm names this change, and it moves toward the customer's own text, so the kind is right. The sentence "No stored document changes reading" in the PR body is true only of the censused sources.
- Other locales: a locale the map has no entry for still reads the catalog, as before. A map equal to the base's map still reads the catalog. No base still reads the catalog. All three are pinned. Right.
- A customization of an installed package can now override the package's bundle with a map entry. With a plain string it already could (`valueOverridesPackagedBase`). So the map case catches up with the string case against the BASE's translation. Right as far as the base's translation goes.
- The same change also lets the map entry beat a translation the paired `.custom` package ships. The string case does not do that. Wrong: see M1.
- `translateDataset` is untouched and pinned (ADR-0149). Dashboard `label` and `description`, widget `description`, global filter labels and report block labels are untouched. Right.
- Gates: every check-run on the head is success or skipped (Test Core 10 shards, Test UI 16 shards, Type Check, Lint, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Docs, Live E2E UI). The docs-drift check named `i18n-standard.mdx`, and the diff updates it.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: minor` matches the rule in AGENTS.md: a `semantic` kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves. Right.
- `@object-ui/app-shell: patch` and `@object-ui/i18n: patch` match: non-protocol changes ship `patch`. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is on both the PR body and the changeset, in the same words. Nothing an author could write is refused, removed or renamed, so there is no narrowing arm to add. The line is right.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is on both. The kind is right. Its text says the entry is served "over the translation bundle" and does not say that this includes the pair's own translations. That gap is M1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev deviation 1, the zh-CN form overlay rows reworded in `metadata-form-zh-cn.ts`: inside the panels the card names. Lane seat's accept.
- Dev deviation 2, seven tests moved to the new wording: lane seat's accept.
- Dev deviation 3, the widget section heading 数据 / Data: lane seat's accept.
- Out-of-scope finding, the English form rows still read the spec's English: no carrier named. It needs a follow-up card or a stated decline from the seat.
- Card item "不做「直接选对象作为数据来源」": held, no such change in the diff.
- SQL push-down: the resolver change is two pure functions over a served document. No query, no id materialisation, no in-app join. Nothing to flag.
- Security: none found.
- #36405 (dashboard in-page edit): no path is shared between the two file lists, so a rebase on this head has no textual conflict. Two notes for it. First, `DashboardWidgetInspector` now reads the served title from `ServedWidgetTextContext`; a host that does not provide it shows the source text in the title box, and an edit there replaces the source string. #36405 should wrap its hosted inspector in that provider. Second, the fix for M1 touches only `i18n-resolver.ts` and its test, which #36405 does not touch, but it moves this head, so #36405 rebases once more.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`

M1 (must-fix) — the new rule lets an inline entry beat a translation the paired `.custom` package ships, which reverses ranks 1 and 2 of ruling record 6631250894. The resolver's own `labelCatalogs` jsdoc states the ruled order: a translation in the pair, then the override's own text, then the base's translation. For a plain string that changed, `catalogFor(catalogs, true)` still reads the pair's catalog first. For a map, when `inlineEntryOverridesPackagedBase` answers true, the lookup is skipped whole, so the pair's catalog is never read. The serving layer does pass `pairBundle` for report and dashboard (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`, the list and item paths). Effect: a declared override with a map entry for zh-CN and a pair translation for the same key showed the pair's translation before this head and shows the inline entry after it. That is a change to what an existing stored document shows, and no line of the declaration, the doc page or the jsdoc names it. No pin covers it: none of the eight new cases passes `pairBundle`. Two ways out. Keep the ruling: treat the slot as changed and read `catalogFor(catalogs, true)`, so the pair's translation still answers first and only the base's translation is skipped, and pin it. Or bring a ruling that amends 6631250894 for these three slots, name it in the `Metadata-protocol` line and the doc page, and pin it.

S1 (should-fix) — `inlineEntryFor` picks an entry by two limbs (exact tag, then bare base tag), while the reader (`resolveI18nLabel`, `pickLocalized`) and the writer (`localeWriteKey`) pick by three limbs with a script stop. The gate and the two ends can disagree. Case one: a `zh-TW` request over `{ default, zh: X }`. The platform table reads bare `zh` as Simplified. The gate answers true through the base tag, so a Traditional reader loses its `zh-TW` bundle text to the Simplified entry. Before this head that reader got the bundle text. Case two: a `zh-TW` request over `{ default, zh: X, zh-HK: Y }`. The gate compares X, and the reader then shows Y, a sibling region, which the jsdoc says never happens. Case three: a session in bare `zh` edits a map that stores `zh-CN`. The writer replaces the `zh-CN` entry, the gate for `zh` finds no entry, and the bundle answers, so the edit is not shown. The fix is one shared selection of "the entry for this locale" for the gate, or a script check before the base-tag limb, plus a pin for a Traditional request.

`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-report.test.ts`

- The eight cases pin the rule as written: the zh-CN entry, the source text, a third locale, the base tag, the equal-map control, the no-base control, the widget title and the dataset scope control. The ablation in the PR body (precedence reverted, 3 red) shows they bind. The missing pins are the ones named in M1 and S1.

`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/servedLabel.ts`

S2 (should-fix) — the file's contract sentence says the server lets the map's entry for the requested language beat the bundle. The resolver does so only when a packaged base is supplied. With no base (a report or dashboard no code package ships, such as a new item in the pair that has its own translation row), `writtenLabel` still stores `{ default: SOURCE, LANG: EDIT }`, the server still serves the bundle text, and the box shows the bundle text again after save. The edit is lost without a message. Card item 5 asks that an edit changes the current language's text. The PR body admits the case but files no follow-up and the jsdoc does not state it. The same loss appears for an override once M1 is fixed the ruling's way and the pair holds a translation for that locale. Fix: decide what the box does when its write will not be served (write the translation row, or say so), or pin the case and correct the sentence, with a follow-up card named.

Nits, no effect on correctness or the contract:

- The jsdoc headers of `translateReport` and `translateDashboard` and the order listed on `labelCatalogs` do not mention the new map rule. Only the inline comments and the new helper do.
- `valueOverridesPackagedBase` says "never a second comparison". The new helper is a second comparison for map values. A line there saying why the map twin is separate, and that the exported predicate and the object fold do not use it, would keep the next reader from merging them.
- A stored override that carries an untouched copy of the package's map goes stale when the package later changes its own inline entry: the old entry now reads as the customer's text. The plain-string rule has the same edge today, so this is the existing class, not a new one.

Design held where I tried to break it: a missing locale answers false and the chain keeps its `en` default; an empty-string entry is not treated as an entry, so it never blanks a label; own-property reads only, so a tag such as `constructor` is not an entry; a widget with no packaged counterpart reads the catalog as before; every consumer of a report label I read in the console goes through a map-aware reader.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-3gbdm3`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对

L1 (L1-e) delta on head `0df531f9fcf2811c84e4bb03b7d502f9df73b836`, card #36373: **ACCEPT**, with one landing condition (body only). This supersedes REWORK 7078823701 (head `e2d307a1`). The contract-tier delta L2 owns the depth reading of the resolver change in `c6ab9f25`. This record reads it at L1.

**Landing condition.** "Findings from the run" items 1–3 are shipped defects the run found and left untouched, and none has a card: I searched, and no card exists for the report page's 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` save.
1. The runtime report 「编辑」 Save on an installed package's report is refused 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. `ReportView`'s save names no package and declares no override, while #36405 gave the dashboard page that route.
2. The report form's 描述 box shows the English source beside a Chinese subtitle.
3. Studio's strip reads 「已选中：Pipeline by Stage」 in a zh-CN session.

Before landing, each needs a card (the seat may file one card or several) and its line in the body needs "carried by #N". Item 4 stays out, per the seat.

**Owed item 1 (live run): closed.**
- At `c6ab9f25`: a fresh backend, HotCRM `689166c` and the branch's console, driven in zh-CN and en-US.
- Every reading I asked for is in the body's table:
  - the heading and subtitle hold with the panel open;
  - the zh-CN panel words, including 数据来源 商机指标 and 总金额 · 合计, which is HotCRM's own label and correctly not 金额;
  - the forbidden-word sweep is clean in both languages, with machine names only on `title`;
  - English has no machine names;
  - Studio uses the same words for the report and for the 阶段管道分布 widget;
  - a self-built untranslated report shows the author's text.
- **The round trip crosses `/meta` both ways:**
  - Studio 定制 → `ensure-customization` 201.
  - `PUT …?mode=draft&package=app.objectstack.hotcrm.custom` with `label: { default, 'zh-CN': '各阶段商机（本公司）' }` and `overrides { package, basedOn }`, answered 200.
  - `publish-drafts` 200.
  - After reload, zh-CN shows the edit, en-US the source, `?locale=zh-CN` and `?locale=en` serve the stored map, and `ja-JP` still reads its bundle.
- Eight live 2× screenshots are present under `repo-objectstack-7/card-36373/`, and the harness shots are deleted.

**Owed item 2 (two sentences): closed.**
- `reports.mdx` and the changeset now scope "the server serves that entry ahead of the translation bundle" to a report with a packaged base. Both say plainly that with no base the bundle stays first and the edit does not show where it has an entry. That is true of `inlineEntryOverridesPackagedBase`.
- After `c6ab9f25` the changeset also says "a translation the paired customization package ships still comes first", and `i18n-standard.mdx` and the `Metadata-protocol: semantic` line say the same. All three match the new resolver: the changed slot reads `catalogFor(changed)`, the pair answers before the entry, and the base's own translation never does.

**The delta's code.**
- **`c6ab9f25` (spec).** The inline entry is now picked the way the panel writes it: exact tag, then the locale's own script for script-split languages (`zh-TW` never takes `zh`), else base tag or sibling region. An entry that differs from the base counts as changed. It is pinned on `pairBundle` for a report and a widget, `zh-TW` over `{ default, zh }` and `{ default, zh, zh-HK }`, and bare `zh` over a stored `zh-CN`. Reverting `i18n-resolver.ts` to `e2d307a1` turns 4 of 30 red.
- **`0df531f9` (app-shell).** `DashboardEditPanel` wraps the hosted inspectors in `ServedWidgetTextContext`, built from `servedWidgetTextOf(published, served)`. `published` is the stored document the edit opened (new `session.published`), and `served` is the page's served dashboard. So on #36405's page, as in Studio, the title box shows the session's language and an edit lands in that language's entry. It is pinned through the real `DashboardView`. With the provider value set to null, the case goes red.
- The changeset now names that host.

**Gates at this head:** 62 success, 11 expected skip, mergeable `clean`. The one `cancelled` row, PR-body guards 137216297574, is superseded on this same head by `success` 137216443203 (13:00:02Z), so it is not a red. Main is merged in with #36405.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0df531f9fcf2811c84e4bb03b7d502f9df73b836`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/spec/src/system/i18n-report.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/servedLabel.ts

Delta review of `e2d307a1..0df531f9`, after record 7078881267 on `e2d307a1`. Inputs read: card #36373 body and its five comments, PR #36420 body and its three comments, the net diff against `main` (33 files, merge base `8a741abd`), the compare of the two heads, and the check-runs on this head. The range holds 30 commits. Three are the PR's own (`ac613f92` docs, `c6ab9f25` resolver, `0df531f9` dashboard page), one is the merge of `main` (`12c41f8f`), and 26 arrived through that merge. The merge brought no hunk to the three scope files: the resolver delta between the two heads is 98 added and 40 removed lines, which is exactly `c6ab9f25`'s. Code outside the diff was read at the head, not reviewed: `ui/packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/servedDashboardText.ts`, and ruling record 6631250894.

Earlier findings:

- M1: closed. A map slot now counts as changed through `slotChanged` and reads `catalogFor(catalogs, true)`, so the pair's translation answers first and only the base's translation is skipped. Three pins pass `pairBundle` (report label with a pair entry, report label with a pair that has no entry for the slot, widget title both ways). The changeset line, the doc page and the jsdoc name the ruling.
- S1: closed. `inlineEntryKeyFor` repeats the reader's and writer's selection with the script stop. I compared it limb by limb with `localizedEntryKey` and `localeWriteKey`: where the gate finds an entry it is the entry the writer replaces, and where the gate finds none the writer adds a new one. The three cases of the finding are pinned (a `zh-TW` request over a bare `zh` entry, a `zh-TW` request over `zh` and `zh-HK`, a bare `zh` session over a `zh-CN` entry).
- S2: closed on the pin-and-sentence arm. The control case is pinned and named, and the header of `servedLabel.ts` now says the stored entry is not always served and lists both cases. The follow-up card it asked for has no number yet: see ③.
- Nits one and two of the earlier record are taken (the three jsdoc headers name the map rule; the helper says why it is a separate function). Nit three stays as the existing class.

### ① Derived judgments

The mirror holds too (request `zh-Hans`, row under `zh-CN`; request `ja-JP`, row under `ja`; request `en-US`, row under `en`).
